newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen easing, retail shares look to rally.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen easing, retail shares look to rally.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open flat to slightly lower but retailers may be in line for a rally after weekend shopping activity offered an early sign that the Christmas shopping season could be a strong one.
"It looks as though the retailers this weekend did extremely well," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
"The market might have a mixed opening but I expect the retailers will probably carry the market to the plus side," he said.

While the apparent burst of shopping activity is good news for retailers, who suffered through a dismal holiday season last year, analysts said it may spell a bit of trouble for the bond market, which has advanced on mounting indications the economy was softening.

"If the consumer is going to be an aggressive spender that doesn't bode well for bonds," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities. "Anything that smacks of a very healthful economy is going to be hurtful to bonds."
The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury fell 7/32 to yield 6.38 percent in early activity.

At 1000 EST/1500 GMT, markets will receive two economic indicators -- October construction spending and the November National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index -- the first installment in a heavy week of data.

Economists expect the construction spending report to show a 1.0 percent decline compared to a 1.9 percent increase in September. The NAPM index is forecast to rise modestly to 50.8 from 50.2 in October.
In Tokyo, stocks skidded, as a rally in blue chip issues stalled. The benchmark Nikkei 225 tumbled 346 points or 1.64 percent to 20,675.
In London, the FTSE 100 slipped 12 points to 4046. U.S. stocks were steady in quiet trade.

The dollar reversed early losses to stand little changed at 113.8 yen Tokyo. The greenback also pushed to a six-week high against the mark and neared its highest level in two years against the Swiss franc.
The December Standard & Poor's 500 index future rose 0.2 of a point to 758.45.

The New York Times Marketplace column writes that Informix Corp is attempting to win market share away from Oracle Corp with release of Universal Server, Informix's new database management software. The software is due for release tomorrow.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column focuses on Revlon Inc, whose shares and bonds have fallen in price over the last month. The column reports that some investors fear financier Ronald Perelman may balk at paying down Revlon's debt.
